item.title: Ana Montana, girlfriend to NBA star LaMelo Ball, arrested on felony drug charges in North Carolina
item.description: Ana Montana faces two felony counts after allegedly filling a Xanax prescription at a Charlotte Walgreens using a doctor's stolen DEA number.
item.content:encoded:
Ana Montana, longtime girlfriend of new Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball, is making off-court headlines for all the wrong reasons after getting hit with felony drug charges in North Carolina.

The 36-year-old Instagram model, whose real name is Analicia Chaves, was booked into a Mecklenburg County jail earlier this week following a months-long police investigation into a Charlotte pharmacy trip that went sideways.

According to court records, the legal trouble traces back to February when Chaves allegedly walked into a local Walgreens to pick up a Xanax prescription.

DOJ CHARGES 10 SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA DEFENDANTS IN LARGEST FEDERAL HEALTHCARE FRAUD CRACKDOWN IN US HISTORY

Law enforcement claims the prescription was filled using a physician's stolen DEA registration and provider credentials.

Authorities officially issued arrest warrants charging her with two felony counts of obtaining controlled substances by fraud or forgery, plus two misdemeanor counts for simple possession of a Schedule IV drug.

Her defense team, led by attorney Matthew Pruden, released a statement insisting Chaves was simply a patient filling an order handed to her by a treating physician. Her legal team maintains she did not forge any paperwork or fabricate prescriptions herself, but rather picked up what she assumed was a valid order at the counter.

The defense statement clarified: "To clarify, the charges allege that a doctor who used a fraudulent DEA registration and NPI number prescribed Alprazolam for Ms. Chaves, and that she used the prescription written by the doctor to obtain the prescribed Alprazolam at a pharmacy."

For Timberwolves and NBA fans keeping track at home, official police records confirm LaMelo Ball isn't named or implicated in any part of the pharmaceutical investigation.

The unexpected legal drama lands right in the middle of a massive year for the couple, who welcomed their baby son, LaOne, back in January before Ball kicked off his offseason routine.

Chaves managed to post bond shortly after being processed, and she is set to face a judge for her court date on Oct. 20.

item.title: ICE arrests illegal alien accused of sexually assaulting children after Fairfax County release: DHS
item.description: DHS says Fairfax County, Virginia, released Oscar Evaristo Nunez, a Honduran immigrant charged with child sex crimes, despite an ICE detainer.
item.content:encoded:
A Honduran illegal immigrant facing multiple child sex crime charges is back in federal custody after authorities in Fairfax County, Virginia, released him from an immigration detainer, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested Oscar Evaristo Nunez Sept. 15 during a targeted enforcement operation, DHS announced Wednesday.

Nunez was initially arrested Aug. 27, 2025, on charges of aggravated sexual battery involving children and offenses related to the non-consensual filming of an undressed minor, according to DHS.

ICE lodged a detainer with the Fairfax County Adult Detention Center two days later, but DHS said local authorities did not honor it and released Nunez without notifying the agency.

GUATEMALAN MAN CHARGED WITH CHILD PORN POSSESSION RELEASED BY FAIRFAX COUNTY DESPITE ICE DETAINER, DHS SAYS

The case has become the latest point of contention between the Trump administration and Virginia officials over cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

"Another criminal illegal alien has been taken off the streets by the brave men and women of ICE with no help from sanctuary politicians in Fairfax County," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a news release. 

"This illegal alien from Honduras had been arrested for child sex crimes in August last year, but Fairfax County refused to honor ICE’s detainer and let this creep back out onto the streets.

"Once again, ICE did the job that these heartless sanctuary politicians won’t do: enforce the law and protect American lives. DHS is calling on Gov. Abigail Spanberger and her fellow sanctuary politicians to stop putting the needs of illegal aliens over the safety of the American people."

‘OUT OF CONTROL’ KILLINGS IN SPANBERGER’S VIRGINIA REACH ‘INSANE’ POINT AS MIGRANT CHARGED IN STABBING SPREE

Spanberger, a Democrat, was not governor when Nunez was arrested, and ICE filed the detainer in August 2025. She took office in January 2026.

Spanberger has moved Virginia away from some forms of state participation in federal immigration enforcement since taking office, including directing state agencies to terminate agreements with ICE under the federal 287(g) program.

A representative for Fairfax County did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

DHS said Nunez illegally entered the U.S. near Arizona around September 2003.

Nunez remains in ICE custody pending immigration proceedings.

item.title: The Rock shares heartfelt words on Pac following AEW star's shocking death at 40
item.description: Dwayne Johnson shared an emotional Instagram video honoring Benjamin Satterley, addressing the AEW locker room and Tony Khan after his death at 40.
item.content:encoded:
Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson offered a heartfelt tribute to Benjamin Satterley and his family after the All Elite Wrestling (AEW) star died on Sunday at the age of 40.

Satterley wrestled in WWE for a few years and was known as Adrian Neville and simply Neville. He was one of the first wrestlers who joined AEW in 2019 and was known as Pac. He won multiple championships in AEW and WWE over the course of his career.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Johnson started his Instagram video by sharing love and his light for the Satterley family.

"I was just so sorry to hear this news. As global as professional wrestling is, as global as WWE is, as much as AEW is growing into this phenomenal wrestling company, and wherever you’re wrestling at around the world, Asia, Latin America, Europe, it doesn’t matter," he continued, "as global as professional wrestling is, we’re still a very tight-knit unit and a tight-knit group because we all share the same DNA.

"And that is our love and our passion for the squared circle and to perform for audiences around the world. And we’re a little crazy, and that’s OK. But when we lose one of our own, it hurts. And when they’re young and so insanely talented, it really, it really f---ing hurts, especially when that life is robbed and you don’t get that opportunity to live a full life."

Johnson addressed AEW owner Tony Khan, fellow wrestler QT Marshall and the AEW locker room, saying he was sorry for their loss.

"For the Satterley family, I wish you love and light as you endure this pain and stay strong."

Johnson is a board member of TKO – the parent company that owns WWE. WWE posted a tribute graphic to Neville before "Monday Night Raw."

AEW was set to have a tribute special of "Dynamite" on Wednesday night in honor of Satterley.

Satterley was found dead in Illinois on Sunday, hours after he performed at All Out.

item.title: Passenger's bizarre use of drinking glass on flight leaves travelers horrified
item.description: Leaving his fellow travelers mortified, an EVA Air business-class passenger was caught on video using a drinking glass to scratch his scalp mid-flight. An etiquette expert weighed in.
item.content:encoded:
An EVA Air business-class passenger left fellow travelers aghast by using a drinking glass to vigorously scratch his scalp while he was seated in the middle of the flight. 

The odd incident aboard a recent flight out of Taiwan on Sept. 24 was all caught on video. 

The man aboard the Boeing 787 Dreamliner apparently decided that the best way to soothe an itchy head was to vigorously massage his scalp using the rim of a drinking glass.

MIDAIR SCARE FORCES PACKED PASSENGER JET INTO EMERGENCY LANDING, TRAVELERS HOSPITALIZED

The bizarre in-seat grooming routine was spotted by a horrified fellow passenger seated directly behind the amateur masseur, according to news outlet Viral Press.

Watching the traveler drag the rim of the upside-down cup through his hair repeatedly and all across his scalp made the witness feel the premium cabin experience had taken a drastic and unexpected turn.

"This is disgusting. It's a cup, not a massage comb," the appalled witness complained.

Losing all appetite for the upcoming meal service, the passenger who recorded the video said, "No one wants to eat your dandruff. I'm really going to vomit," Viral Press reported.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The EVA Air flight landed safely, NewsFlare reported. 

The company, headquartered in Taiwan, was founded in 1989, according to its website. 

Texas-based etiquette expert Diane Gottsman told Fox News Digital that "using a glass to scratch [one's] head is completely inappropriate," particularly while in public and surrounded by other people. 

"Any time you see someone scratching themselves with an object, or even scratching themselves with their fingers in a public area — it’s unappealing and somewhat alarming," she added.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

In recent years, several flyers have complained that fellow passengers are crossing the line when it comes to public-facing behavior aboard planes.

In March 2026, a passenger was slammed for putting feet up on a window.

At the time, a Reddit user blasted the other traveler.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"First time experiencing the feet in my face in five years. Travel monthly. In first class, and this lady put her feet on my arm rest. I shoved them off."

The writer continued, "And five minutes later, she has them up on her window. At least she has socks on. But come on, people! It’s a 4.5 hour flight."

Said Gottsman, "When you’re in your home, you are in a private space. [But] when you are out in public, there are different standards because you are around other people and must be aware of your surroundings and the comfort level of others."

item.title: Anticipation builds as MIke Tomlin prepares to unveil his Minecraft city that's 12 years in the making
item.description: Mike Tomlin reveals he's been secretly building a "Minecraft" city for twelve years, calling it therapeutic during his high-pressure coaching career.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 NFL season is the first without Mike Tomlin somewhere on the sidelines in decades.

And while the former Steelers coach has moved into the world of TV broadcasting, he's about to become a big deal in a corner of the internet no one would've expected a few months ago.

"Minecraft" streaming.

That's right, the longtime Steelers head coach is about to let fans into the blockified city he has been crafting for the last twelve years.

"It was therapeutic for me," Tomlin said in a video posted to social media. "It allowed me to detach from the pressures and the reality of life. Kind of my secret obsession, and so let's take you all through it."

The video then teased the release of a full video on Tomlin's YouTube channel, which showed an aerial view of a city that had a baseball field, streets, and even buildings with what looked to my eye to be HVAC equipment on the roof.

Mike means business, and I love it.

BREAKING UP TROY AIKMAN AND JOE BUCK WOULD BE A BIG MISTAKE FOR ESPN | BOBBY BURACK

The "NBC Sunday Night Football" analyst revealed in an interview around the start of the season that he was a big fan of the building game that has become a cultural phenomenon over the years.

It makes so much sense to me.

RAMS COACH SEAN MCVAY'S '60 MINUTES' INTERVIEW REVEALS WHY YOU SHOULDN'T FIND YOUR IDENTITY IN YOUR JOB

Being an NFL coach is such a high-pressure job with a lot of noise. How better to get a break from that than by focusing all of your attention on the 8-bit stadium you're trying to construct?

I can't think of one, and it's a pretty healthy way to tune everything out and get yourself focused on the present.

If you're wondering how he was able to handle being an NFL coach for so long, well, for twelve of those years, this is your answer.

Now that Tomlin isn't leading an NFL team anymore, he's got more time to devote to Tomlinburg (or whatever he calls it), and I expect it to be looking like Tokyo in a few months.

item.title: California superintendent candidate calls out teachers union, says she's a 'real threat' to 'socialist agenda'
item.description: Leaked audio captured a teachers union calling Sonja Shaw a "real threat" as the California Teachers Association spends millions backing her opponent.
item.content:encoded:
Conservative California superintendent candidate Sonja Shaw told Fox News Digital Tuesday she would not back down from confronting the United Teachers Los Angeles union (UTLA) after a circulated video allegedly showed a union leader calling Shaw a "real threat" and warning that her election "would cause a huge problem for us."

Shaw, the president of the Chino Valley Unified School District board, pointed to Los Angeles student achievement scores as she accused UTLA of protecting the education establishment rather than focusing on academic outcomes.

"I’m not surprised the Los Angeles teachers union sees me as a threat," Shaw said in a statement to Fox News Digital. 

"More than half of their students still can’t read at grade level, and nearly two-thirds can’t do math. Instead of working to help those kids, UTLA has fought to keep parents in the dark, excused failure and protected the system that produced these results."

NATION’S LARGEST TEACHERS UNION UNDER FIRE AS CONTROVERSIAL AGENDA PUTS CENTURY-OLD FEDERAL CHARTER AT RISK

California’s latest official assessment results lend context to Shaw’s criticism of Los Angeles Unified’s academic performance. 

In 2025, 46.46% of LAUSD students met or exceeded the state standard in English language arts and 36.76% met or exceeded the standard in mathematics, according to California Department of Education testing data. That meant roughly 53.5% did not meet the ELA standard and 63.2% did not meet the math standard.

Shaw said the criticism described in the video would not change her approach to the statewide race.

"If putting children and families first is a ‘huge problem’ for their agenda, that tells you everything you need to know. I won’t back down," she said. "They just admitted it. I’m a ‘real threat’ to their socialist agenda. Parents over politics. Kids over ideology. Girls over boys in their sports and locker rooms. Keep calling me a threat. I’ll keep being one."

WATCHDOG REPORT EXPOSES TEACHERS UNION 'POLITICAL MACHINE' FUNNELING MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO LIBERAL CAUSES

In the clip, shared by Corey DeAngelis, a research fellow at The Heritage Foundation, a woman describes Shaw as a "real threat" and discusses efforts to prevent a "MAGA lady" from taking charge of public education.

The woman then warned about what Shaw taking office would mean for the organization.

"That would cause a huge problem for us," the woman said.

The California Post reported the speaker was Julie Van Winkle, the UTLA AFT vice president.

HOUSE GOP LAUNCHES PROBE INTO 5 MAJOR LABOR UNIONS OVER DEM SPENDING DESPITE MAGA MEMBERSHIP BASE

DeAngelis told Fox News Digital he viewed the purported criticism as evidence that Shaw was threatening teachers unions’ political influence.

"This leaked audio is the best endorsement Sonja Shaw could’ve ever received. When a power-hungry teachers union that fights to protect itself at the expense of kids calls you an existential threat to their socialist agenda, you’re officially over the target," he said.

UTLA has publicly endorsed Shaw’s opponent, San Diego Unified School District Board President Richard Barrera, for California superintendent of public instruction. The union says Barrera has a "proven commitment" to working with educators and families and called for a superintendent who would work with unions on education funding.

Organized labor has also spent millions supporting Barrera. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

California Secretary of State data compiled by CalMatters showed the California Teachers Association Independent Expenditure Committee had spent $5,057,539 supporting Barrera as of Sept. 15, compared with $10,000 in reported outside spending supporting Shaw.

Los Angeles County Republican Party Chair Roxanne Hoge also pointed Fox News Digital to a post from Saturday on X tying the controversy to Gov. Gavin Newsom’s recent overhaul of the superintendent’s authority.

"We knew [Sonja Shaw] was causing good trouble when [Gavin Newsom] stripped the office she's running for of most of its power," she said.

Fox News Digital reached out to UTLA and Newsom's office for comment.

item.title: ‘We beat Disney, Fauci, Soros’: Ron DeSantis unleashes ‘Florida model’ in hard-hitting midterm rally
item.description: Ron DeSantis headlined a rally for Navy veteran Dan Green, a GOP candidate in Florida's 9th district seeking to oust incumbent Darren Soto
item.content:encoded:
Pitching his administration’s conservative record as a national blueprint for Capitol Hill, Gov. Ron DeSantis rallied Republicans in Osceola County Tuesday night, portraying Navy veteran Dan Green’s bid for Florida’s 9th Congressional District as part of a broader push to bring aggressive Florida-style governance to Washington.

Speaking before a crowd in St. Cloud, south of Orlando, DeSantis pointed to his administration's high-profile battles on education policy, state spending reductions and corporate pushback and urged voters to bring that same combative, policy-driven mandate to the halls of Congress.

SOCIAL MEDIA ERUPTS AFTER DESANTIS GIVES ‘SOROS’ PROTESTER A PIECE OF HIS MIND: ‘AIN’T MY FIRST RODEO’

"I will say that I'm looking forward to y'all getting the congressman elected that has served this country and that has served for the right reasons. Now, I am a big believer that we need term limits for members of Congress. But until we do that, you can show your current guy the term limit by kicking him out of office.

"So, I think what we need is what we've done in Florida. It can be a model for people like Dan going to Washington, other states, you name it, because it's not just about peacocking and putting social media press releases out and never getting anything done. We have fought every big fight that there has been to fight in the state of Florida, and we have won every big fight that there is to fight in Florida."

DeSantis rallied the conservative faithful with a recap, alleging major victories over left-wing institutions, agencies and agendas.

"Just think about it. We beat Dr. Fauci on COVID. We beat Disney on gender ideology. We beat Soros on crime by removing two of his prosecutors. We beat Martha's Vineyard on illegal immigration.

"We just beat the Muslim Brotherhood by banning Sharia law. We beat the teachers unions by enacting universal school choice for all Florida families. We beat SEIU by doing paycheck protection.

"Every single time there was a fight, we would beat and win the fights. And that's ultimately what it's all about. Because leadership — when it's popular, when it's easy — anyone can do that. 'I'll just go with the flow,' all this other stuff. It really matters when it is tough and when you're going to face arrows."

TRUMP'S HANDPICKED DESANTIS SUCCESSOR WINS CROWDED GOP PRIMARY FOR FLORIDA GOVERNOR

DeSantis repeatedly emphasized that his top priority was sticking to the courage of his convictions, not seeking political expediency or going along to get along.

"I remember during COVID, I was doing things, and people said, 'Oh, he's not shutting down the beaches. Why does he have these people in school?' And all this other stuff. You know, people come after you, and a lot of people told me that I was frittering away my governorship, that I wouldn't be able to win in '22, and all this other stuff. I don't know if that was true. Who knows, right? 

"But when you get in a position to lead, you either do it or you should just sit down. My job was not to be worried about my own political hide. My job was to be worried about protecting the liberty, jobs, and businesses of the people I was elected to serve. So, we started the fire, and we gave them his right."

It is clear that the two-term governor considers his famed battle with Disney to be a particular feather in his cap.

"Nobody in the history of the state had ever taken on Disney in anything. A lot of people told me I was making a mistake," DeSantis said.

"But the reality is, do we want a society in which our 6-year-olds are being told they can change genders, or do we want a society rooted in truth? If you want a society rooted in truth, even if the biggest, most powerful corporation in the state is against you, you've got to stand up and you've got to fight. And we fought, and we won."

As the federal debt has topped a staggering $40 trillion, DeSantis made the case that he has taken the state on a markedly divergent course.

"Just look at the results. For four straight years, Florida has reduced its budget. Is any other state in the country reducing spending? We've done it four years in a row," DeSantis said.

"I was just able to announce today if you take all of Florida's debt for all of our history up until the time I became governor, just in my tenure, we will retire 54% of the state's debt, more than cutting it in half. 

"We've been ranked No. 1 for education freedom, and our public university system is ranked No. 1. We have the lowest in-state tuition of any state in the United States, and it's the exact same cost today to students and families that it was the day I took office. 

"It did not go up one penny under my tenure. Is there anything else that didn't go up? The dollar menu at McDonald's is all $2.99 now. Everything else has gone up, but that has not gone up."

And DeSantis touts Florida as a national leader in lowering taxes for its citizens and called for voters to back Amendment 3 in Florida, which would pave the way for elimination of non-school property taxes.

"If you look at tax relief, we've done $10 billion over my tenure — more than anyone. Some of it is permanent, like no tax on baby items, back-to-school items and no tax on business rent. But, really, the big enchilada is going to be on the ballot in November when you have a chance on Amendment 3 to vote yourself more control over your own home and not let them tax you to death. So vote yes on 3.

As Republicans face headwinds heading into the midterms in a little over a month, DeSantis drew a parallel between this year's election, and the 2018 election, which propelled him to the governor's mansion by a narrow margin.

"We've done all this stuff, but I think the lesson is this: When I won eight years ago, it was kind of similar to how it is now. People were saying it was a ‘blue year.’ There was a lot of wind in the face of Republican candidates," DeSantis recalled.

"A lot of people thought Florida was a swing state — that we were purple — where one point had decided all these races for the previous decade. A lot of people didn't think I could even win given those circumstances. And even if I won, they said, 'Well, the state's going to go blue. You've got all these people moving from Puerto Rico, the Northeast, anything.' So, I'm running. It wasn't easy, and we won."

DeSantis maintains he has never taken a poll as a means to determine a position on an issue.

"It was a close race, so I had a choice to make: Do I try to tiptoe around the tulips, not offend anybody, and just try to walk this tight line? Or do I say, 'You know what? I won the election. I got 100% of the executive power, and I didn't get elected to follow. I got elected to lead,'" DeSantis said.

"So, I am going to fly the banner of bold colors, not pale pastels. I'm going to do what I believe in. I am not going to take any polls. I have not to this day ever polled a single issue in my entire time as governor.

"The reason is simple. … It depends on how you ask the question, right? I can tweak the words and get a different result. But also, what does a poll actually mean? Like Popeye said, ‘I am what I am,’ right?"

item.title: Phillies force Game 3 as Kyle Schwarber, Bryce Harper go back-to-back and Alec Bohm homers in 10th vs Braves
item.description: Alec Bohm's 10th-inning home run forced a decisive Game 3 after Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper launched back-to-back blasts to erase a deficit.
item.content:encoded:
Game 2 of the National League Wild Card Series was deadlocked at 3-3 Wednesday afternoon before Alec Bohm delivered Philadelphia's biggest swing. His two-out homer in the 10th inning lifted the Phillies to a 4-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves and forced a winner-take-all Game 3.

The Phillies had trailed 3-1 before Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper hit back-to-back homers in the seventh. Harper's blast came one inning after he committed a costly fielding error.

Andrew Painter then took over. The regular-season starter worked three scoreless innings to protect Philadelphia's taxed bullpen, stranded two runners in the 10th and struck out Dominic Smith after the Phillies won an ABS challenge.

MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL DESPERATELY NEEDS TO FIX ITS TERRIBLE POSTSEASON SCHEDULING PRACTICES

Playing under traditional extra-inning rules that don't include designated runners at second base like in the regular season, Bohm delivered his third career postseason home run, a 357-foot shot to right field off right-hander Didier Fuentes.

The Phillies will try to continue their postseason dominance over the Braves in Thursday's Game 3. Philadelphia beat Atlanta in the 1993 NLCS and the 2022 and 2023 NLDS.

In the seventh, Drake Baldwin's double glanced off Harper's glove in right field, driving in Sean Murphy to give Atlanta a 2-1 lead. Harper, who resumed playing the outfield late this season for the first time since 2022, got a poor jump and was leaping for the ball near the warning track. He was not charged with an error. Matt Olson added a sacrifice fly.

"Probably should have been caught, obviously," Harper said.

The Phillies pulled even with eighth-inning home runs by Schwarber and Harper off Dylan Lee, the winning pitcher in the Braves' 5-3 opening win on Tuesday. Schwarber’s drive carried 447 feet and Harper followed with a 418-foot drive.

Tyler Mahle allowed one run on six hits in seven innings for Atlanta. Cristopher Sánchez allowed three runs in 6 2/3 innings for Philadelphia while throwing a career-high 116 pitches.

The start time for the decisive Game 3 has not yet been determined. The Braves announced that MLB will schedule the game for either 2:15 p.m. ET or 8:15 p.m. ET in Atlanta, with the final time dependent on the conclusion of the other three Wild Card Series Game 2 matchups tonight.

item.title: Fetal tissue supplier billed $765 procurement fee per organ, warns records could imply illegal sales: records
item.description: Records obtained by David Daleiden’s Center for Medical Progress show UCLA purchase orders tied $765 procurement service fees to individual liver and thymus specimens
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Newly obtained public records show Cercle Allocation Services billed a UCLA research operation a $765 procurement service fee tied to each individual liver and thymus specimen, while warning in internal correspondence that certain billing language could improperly imply the tissue itself was being sold.

The records, obtained from UCLA through a California Public Records Act request made on behalf of Center for Medical Progress founder David Daleiden, include purchase orders and correspondence between the university and Cercle Allocation Services.

An internal UCLA order form identifies the purchasing operation as part of the David Geffen School of Medicine’s Division of Hematology-Oncology and references the "Mouse Core." UCLA redacted the names and other identifying information of researchers from the record.

The records reviewed by Fox News Digital do not establish that UCLA or its researchers, procurement personnel or other employees engaged in illegal or unethical conduct with the transactions.

'DRUG-DEALING' NETWORK SHIELDED BY BLUE STATES TARGETED IN SCOTUS CHALLENGE

One UCLA purchase order lists seven individually numbered liver and thymus specimens at a $765 unit amount apiece, totaling $5,355. Another lists five specimens from Aug. 18, 2023, each carrying the same $765 amount, for a total of $3,825. Additional purchase orders reflect the same per-specimen amount.

Cercle objected to the purchase orders’ tax treatment and asked UCLA to reissue them, telling the university that the charges reflected procurement services and that sales tax should not be applied. Cercle said tax language could improperly imply that the specimens themselves were being sold.

Cercle does supply human fetal tissue for biomedical research. Peer-reviewed scientific literature has identified the company as the source of human fetal liver tissue used by researchers, providing independent evidence of the type of procurement business described by CMP.

SUPREME COURT UNANIMOUSLY SLAPS DOWN BLUE STATE TARGETING PRO-LIFE GROUP

CMP identified the liver and thymus specimens in the UCLA purchase orders as fetal tissue. Fox News Digital has not independently verified that the tissue associated with these specific purchase orders was fetal. The purchase orders identify the organs by type, sample number and date but do not describe them as fetal.

The records do not establish that the payments were illegal. Cercle characterized the money as fees for procurement services rather than payments for the tissue itself.

But correspondence shows the company was particularly concerned about how those payments were described.

"The overriding issue is the use of terminology that we must not use due to their improper implication that we are selling taxable items, which we are not," a Cercle accounts manager wrote in September 2023. "Due to the nature of our business, we must be very careful and clear that we invoice fees for our procurement services."

The same email said notations referring to sales tax would imply Cercle was "selling the items received," which the company said were "illegal to sell." Cercle instead instructed UCLA that purchase orders should authorize payment for its services while tying individual sample numbers and dates to a unit amount of $765.

The correspondence shows UCLA subsequently prepared revised purchase orders after Cercle objected to the tax language.

One Cercle email said a July invoice totaling $5,355 for procurements on three dates had already been "processed and paid." The company also asked UCLA to replace other purchase orders containing tax language, including one covering five procurements from Aug. 18 worth a combined $3,825.

Federal law prohibits knowingly acquiring, receiving or otherwise transferring human fetal tissue for "valuable consideration," if the transfer affects interstate commerce, while allowing "reasonable payments" associated with transportation, implantation, processing, preservation, quality control or storage.

The records reviewed by Fox News Digital do not establish that Cercle or UCLA violated that prohibition.

Daleiden contends the documents raise questions about whether the uniform $765 charges represented permissible reimbursement for procurement-related costs.

HAWLEY SENDS CRIMINAL REFERRAL OF 'LEFT-WING DARK-MONEY' GROUP OVER MAILED ABORTION DRUGS

He pointed to the uniform $765 amount UCLA assigned to individual specimens on the purchase orders, including multiple organs listed on the same date. Daleiden told Fox News Digital he believes the structure raises questions about whether the payments reflected the procurement-related costs permitted under federal law.

Documents reviewed by Fox News Digital do not contain Cercle’s invoices or underlying cost calculations and do not establish whether the $765 amount exceeded reasonable procurement-related expenses.

Daleiden also said UCLA did not produce Cercle’s invoices in response to the public records request.

The May 2025 request sought the original and most recent materials associated with UCLA IRB No. 11-002504 and records and communications from 2023 forward between the authors of a specified UCLA study and Advanced Bioscience Resources or Cercle. The request covered records, including emails, text messages, notes and fetal tissue logs.

UCLA later said its departments had completed their search and that the September 2026 production represented the final batch of non-exempt responsive records. The university said it redacted certain researcher identities because of concerns about threats and harassment involving sensitive research.

Records also show the UCLA-Cercle relationship continued into 2025.

A February 2025 Cercle ticket involving UCLA was titled "Liver and brain." Cercle responded March 3 that it had been "unable to fulfill your request today" and canceled the ticket. The records do not specify that the requested tissue was fetal or establish that any brain tissue was ultimately procured or transferred.

Daleiden has spent years investigating fetal tissue procurement after CMP released undercover videos involving Planned Parenthood officials in 2015. His recording operation later became the subject of a California criminal case.

Kamala Harris’ office opened the investigation while she was California attorney general. Charges were later filed under Attorney General Xavier Becerra. In April 2026, a California judge dismissed the final charge and expunged the case.

The records reviewed by Fox News Digital do not establish that the UCLA-Cercle transactions violated federal law. UCLA and Cercle have not been accused or charged by authorities with illegal conduct in the transactions reflected in the public records obtained by CMP.

UCLA and Cercle Allocation Services did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

item.title: WNBA commentator Sydney Colson physically restrained after going after Fever fan following A'ja Wilson mess
item.description: Video footage captures Sydney Colson lunging at a spectator as an Amazon staffer physically restrains her during a WNBA playoff game Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Former Indiana Fever player and Amazon Prime commentator Sydney Colson lost complete control during Tuesday’s WNBA playoff game between the Las Vegas Aces and Fever, lunging at a spectator while a staff member physically restrained her.

The chaos began when Aces star A’ja Wilson overreacted to a fan who simply pointed at her and shouted, "It’s on you!" following a foul call. Wilson marched two rows deep into the baseline seats to confront him, earning a technical foul for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Instead of maintaining professional distance as a credentialed media member, Colson and fellow Amazon analyst Theresa Plaisance (also a podcast co-host with Wilson) left their courtside seats and inserted themselves into the altercation.

As arena personnel escorted Colson and Plaisance away from the baseline, a spectator in a red Fever shirt directed a comment toward them. Plaisance pointed back and called him a "little b***h boy." Colson then continued pushing aggressively toward the fan as an Amazon staffer struggled to hold her back. Video footage captured her shouting, "Who do you think you are? B—-, who the f— do you think you are?"

Colson spent the 2025 season in Indiana before exiting the franchise. Ever since packing her bags, taking public cheap shots at her former team has become a habit.

Right on script, the broadcast team immediately scrambled to run cover for Wilson.

Prime Video analyst LaChina Robinson insisted on-air that "something was said" simply because Wilson does not normally react that way.

Aces coach Becky Hammon predictably chimed in, claiming she had never seen Wilson react like that and assuming her star felt "deeply disrespected."

Wilson doubled down after the game, apologizing to her teammates for picking up the technical foul while insisting the fan’s conduct crossed the line.

"I don’t know if you guys know me, but I don’t get into the bulls—," Wilson told reporters. "I try to play my game, keep it pushing. But if I’m just walking, because I just got the foul, I’m chilling, and if I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don’t give a damn what you said. I don’t give a damn how you said it. The tone, that is unacceptable."

Wilson went further, complaining about how the fan was allowed to return to his seat after security reviewed the incident.

"And how he gets back in the game because they said he didn’t do anything? Of course he did, and that’s fine," she said.

item.title: Gavin Newsom seeks counsel from ‘master’ Bill Clinton as he plots Project 2029
item.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom said former President Bill Clinton calls him late at night to discuss policy and strategy as the California governor builds his Project 2029 framework.
item.content:encoded:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom is turning to a former president for political inspiration as speculation builds around his potential 2028 White House bid.

"I don’t have a problem fighting," Newsom told Vanity Fair when discussing a potential 2028 presidential run. "Nor do I have a problem getting roughed up and getting back up. I’ve been road tested. It’s not small ball out here in California."

Newsom, who is nearing the end of his second and final term as California governor, named former President Bill Clinton his political model, telling Vanity Fair Clinton is a "master of his craft."

GAVIN NEWSOM SAYS HE WON'T RUN FOR PRESIDENT IN 2028 IF KAMALA HARRIS RUNS

"I watch videos of Clinton. I seek his counsel, his advice, and even in his absence, do that. I’ve been a student of his from day one," he told the outlet.

Newsom said the relationship extends beyond admiration from afar, revealing that he and Clinton frequently speak late at night about policy, political strategy and how to address California's challenges.

"He calls me late at night, wanting to talk about it, and he goes, ‘I’ve been thinking just nonstop about this. I just think you represent what they fear,’" Newsom said.

He praised Clinton as an exceptional problem solver despite scrutiny surrounding the former president’s past association with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and a sex scandal with White House intern Monica Lewinsky. Clinton has denied knowing about Epstein’s crimes or engaging in wrongdoing.

BILL CLINTON REVEALS HOW HE FEELS ABOUT UPCOMING MIDTERMS AFTER SOCIALIST VICTORIES

"[There is] no greater problem solver in that respect than Bill Clinton, in my mind. Master of his craft. Next-level," Newsom said.

The California governor's embrace of Clinton also comes as he navigates an evolving Democratic Party, where democratic socialist figures have gained prominence alongside the more moderate political tradition Clinton once represented.

The governor made it clear he does not associate himself with the Democratic "establishment," instead casting himself as a political "disrupter."

"I’m notoriously a disrupter at heart," he told Vanity Fair. "I’ve never been for the status quo. Quite the contrary. I have a record that consistently challenges the status quo, and I tend to take risks to a degree that few elected officials do."

NEWSOM TELLS DEMOCRATS TO BE IN THE 'ADDITION NOT SUBTRACTION' BUSINESS WITH SOCIALISTS

Newsom, who said he won't run in 2028 if former Vice President Kamala Harris does, also discussed a 36-page book he is writing, full of policy ideas for what he calls Project 2029, a governing framework modeled in name after MAGA's Project 2025.

"No one touches these," Newsom said about his pages of ideas. "These are my own little version. This is just policy, not narrative, the kinds of things we need to do: zoning reform, corporate tax, junk-fee stuff, new domestic strategies and tariffs, preschool things, a cap on childcare, family leave, paid sick leave, child tax credits, industrial decarbonization, anti-monopoly stuff, immigration, whistleblower protections."

Democratic strategist Doug Friednash told Fox News Digital Newsom is wise to take after Clinton, while warning if the Democratic Party continues to move to the far left, it could make the 2028 Democratic nominee "toxic."

GAVIN NEWSOM EXPRESSES 'OPENNESS' TO PACKING SCOTUS, CALLS ELECTORAL COLLEGE SYSTEM 'PERVERTED'

"At a time when the Democratic Party brand is incredibly unpopular with Americans, Newsom would be wise to take a page out of Bill Clinton’s playbook recognizing that Democrats need to appeal beyond its progressive left," Friednash said. 

"Newsom’s challenge will be authentically casting himself as a disrupter when he has spent decades as part of the California political establishment."

Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff agreed with Friednash, arguing that Clinton understood the importance of putting the country’s necessities over those of activists or party leaders, an instinct he says Newsom is "clearly trying to learn."

"Clinton’s lesson was that successful Democrats could move the party in new directions without losing touch with voters who did not speak the language of the activist left," Schroff told Fox News Digital. 

"Newsom seems to understand that distinction. The harder question is whether he can actually pull it off."

item.title: Sean McVay says NFL has admitted officials made major mistake that probably cost the Rams a loss vs Denver
item.description: Sometimes NFL officials get it wrong. Sean McVay says the league admitted the pass interference penalty on Josh Wallace was not the right call.
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes NFL officials get it right. Sometimes they get it wrong. And when that happens, the NFL often acknowledges the mistake to its teams, as it did with the Los Angeles Rams and their controversial pass interference call against the Denver Broncos.

The NFL has apparently admitted its officials were wrong to call pass interference on Rams defensive back Josh Wallace in the Sunday Night Football game.

NFL'S MOST DEBATED WEEK 3 CALL HAS PEOPLE WONDERING HOW TO DEFY GRAVITY WHEN HITTING PATRICK MAHOMES

That call almost certainly cost the Rams the game.

Rams coach Sean McVay said Wednesday he was told by the league that Wallace should not have been called for defensive pass interference on that play.

Huge if true.

The NFL did not immediately respond to an email from OutKick seeking confirmation that the league acknowledged the officiating mistake to McVay. So we're going on his word only.

But the coach has no reason to lie.

The penalty against Wallace was a double whammy. It negated what would have been a potential game-sealing interception with 1:09 remaining to play and the Rams leading 26-23.

The blown call instead resulted in pass interference against Wallace and the Rams. That gave the Broncos a first-and-goal situation at the Los Angeles 7-yard line, setting up a touchdown six plays later and a 30-26 Broncos win.

It should be noted that Wallace did indeed make contact with Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant.

But in a league that often prefers to let players decide games in the final minutes rather than having officials determine the outcome, referee Bill Vinovich's crew stepped in, and they pretty much helped decide the game.

Regardless of the mistake, the NFL is not awarding the Rams anything other than maybe some satisfaction. The Rams still carry the loss in the standings and the Broncos keep their victory.

Kudos to the NFL for admitting its officials were wrong, especially since league officials had to know that telling McVay would be as if broadcasting it nationwide. He wasn't going to treat that communication as a secret.

Immediately after the controversial call, McAulay was asked to chime in on the broadcast and told everyone what he saw. There was no interference.

item.title: Mamdani's taxpayer-funded influencer army accused of plotting pressure campaign against NYC CEOs
item.description: Senior aides to Mayor Zohran Mamdani reportedly discussed mobilizing a 200-plus influencer network against top CEOs and business leaders in New York City.
item.content:encoded:
Senior officials in New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's administration are reportedly plotting a coordinated social media pressure campaign against some of the city's most powerful business leaders, looking to mobilize a 200-plus influencer network run through City Hall.

Mamdani's network of social media creators working for him first drew scrutiny earlier this month after the Columbia Journalism Review revealed that City Hall was communicating with more than 200 influencers through an encrypted Signal group called "NYC Creators Announcements." 

Fox News Digital subsequently reported that members receive daily talking points, videos and other updates from the administration, while also being offered access to events and city officials.

MAMDANI’S ‘MASS ENGAGEMENT’ OFFICE DRAWS FIRE OVER PLANS TO BUILD INFLUENCE BEYOND CITY HALL: ‘NYC IS DONE’

Now, two sources briefed on the effort told the New York Post that senior City Hall aides have discussed mobilizing the influencer network against New York business executives, including leaders of the Partnership for New York City, an influential nonprofit representing the city's business leaders and largest employers. 

Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla and Related Companies CEO Jeff Blau have also been floated as potential targets, according to the Post.

The reported strategy centers on "blindsid[ing]" Partnership for New York City President and CEO Steven Fulop, who took over the organization earlier this year, with one source telling the Post that aides viewed the leadership transition as an opportunity to "go at CEOs."

"They want to punch Fulop in the face," the source told The Post.

Fulop, however, told Fox News he personally spoke with Mamdani after the report and that the mayor, his communications director and political director all denied plans to target business executives. Fulop said the Partnership would take Mamdani "at his word" while remaining "vigilant and watchful" but noted if he continued down this path there could be "huge repercussions in a bad way." 

Mamdani spokesperson Dora Pekec, meanwhile, called the Post's report "categorically false" and "a complete lie," though the Post reported that she declined to identify specific inaccuracies in its account.

The Mamdani administration's use of influencers and Signal had already drawn scrutiny before the latest report this week from the New York Post.

Reinvent Albany, a government watchdog focused on transparency and accountability, has said it supports city agencies using paid social media influencers to promote government programs but opposes city officials using instant-messaging apps such as Signal for official communications.

MAMDANI SPARKS FEARS OF VIOLENCE AFTER DOXING WEALTHY NYC PROPERTY OWNERS: 'OUTRIGHT DANGEROUS'

In testimony before the New York City Council earlier this month, the group warned that the city still lacks a practical way for agency Freedom of Information Law officers to archive or retrieve official records created on apps such as Signal.

"Even now, in 2026, the City of New York has not developed a practical way for official records created by these apps to be archived or retrieved by agency FOIL officers," Reinvent Albany testified.

The watchdog has called for legislation clarifying that electronic and instant messages constituting public records must be preserved and easily retrievable, while also proposing disclosure requirements for influencers paid to promote city messaging.

NYC MAYOR MAMDANI CALLS THREAT OF RICH PEOPLE LEAVING NYC OVER TAXES 'IMAGINED'

The alleged effort to go after NYC's CEOs comes as Mamdani continues to push for higher taxes on wealthy New Yorkers and corporations to fund his agenda and address the city's budget challenges.

Mamdani called earlier this year for a 2% personal income tax increase on New Yorkers earning $1 million or more, alongside an increase in the corporate tax rate. While those proposals did not make it into this year's budget, Mamdani has continued to publicly back both.

"I've been very open and honest about my vision, whether it be fast and free buses or whether it be higher personal income taxes on the wealthiest New Yorkers or the most profitable corporations," Mamdani said in May.

The mayor did secure a new pied-à-terre tax on luxury second homes owned by non-city residents, which his administration projects will generate roughly $500 million annually. 

The measure was dealt a legal setback Tuesday, however, when a Staten Island judge ordered the administration to scrap its initial rollout and restart the process after finding the city failed to follow required procedures before sending tax notices. The ruling did not strike down the tax itself, and Mamdani's administration vowed to continue fighting for the surcharge.

Matt Rauschenbach, a Mamdani spokesman, defended the surcharge as a "basic principle of fairness," arguing that owners of luxury second homes should contribute toward the city services they benefit from.

item.title: Craig Carton blasts WNBA, A'Ja Wilson over fan confrontation: 'This league can't get out of its own way'
item.description: A'ja Wilson's altercation with a front-row fan during the Las Vegas Aces vs. Indiana Fever playoff game sparked a heated debate on social media.
item.content:encoded:
The latest scandal to rock the WNBA has made the rounds all throughout social media and the internet.

A'Ja Wilson, the four-time WNBA MVP, was involved in an altercation with a fan during the Las Vegas Aces' playoff matchup with the Indiana Fever, and her reaction has everyone buzzing.

The Aces center took exception to a man in the front row pointing at her after she committed a foul, marching toward him before being restrained by officials.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Wilson was assessed a technical foul and the fan was later cleared of any wrongdoing, but public reaction is split on whether he was in the right for his actions.

OutKick's very own Craig Carton weighed in on the situation, and as you can expect, he had some harsh words for Wilson and the WNBA in general.

"What did the guy do," Carton asks. "Was he being a toxic masculine figure?"

As Carton points out, the guy is just out with his wife or girlfriend, trying to enjoy a WNBA game, and is getting vilified for having the audacity to point at Wilson.

WNBA REFS MISS OPPORTUNITY TO EJECT A'JA WILSON OVER MELTDOWN, ENTERING STANDS

"The crazy thing about this is the guy did nothing wrong," he explains. "They review the videotape and despite the announcers that are broadcast the game saying he must have said something racist, he must be a racist, he must be a race baiter, or he said something offensive, none of that was true."

It's worth pointing out that this man spent his hard earned money to sit on the floor of a WNBA game, which wouldn't be something a racist would do, a point Carton agrees with.

DAN DAKICH BLASTS A'JA WILSON OVER FAN INCIDENT IN PLAYOFF LOSS TO THE FEVER

"Well, he's not a racist. That's why he's there. He's trying to enjoy the sport that he hears a lot about."

This is just the latest in a long list of examples of the WNBA alienating the fans that continue to show up despite the league's best efforts to ostracize them.

"This is what the WNBA does they eat their own," Carton said. "The WNBA has gotta be the most incompetent league on the planet. It's a circus. It's a sideshow."

"You want more of those guys," he continues. "You can't attack that guy into the silly phrase of oh that's toxic masculinity. No, that's called a good fan. You need more of those people, not less of those people."

The Fever would go on to win the game 99-89 to tie the series and force a win-or-go-home scenario on Thursday, but as Carton says, no one cares about that.

"Once again nobody's discussing what happened on the court. I can tell you as I sit here right now, I couldn't tell you who won the game. I have no idea who won the game. I also don't care. But it's another example of this league not being able to get out of its own way."

item.title: Arizona State hockey coach placed on paid leave as investigation into tragic workout continues
item.description: Arizona State University placed hockey coach Greg Powers on paid leave as the investigation into a workout that left a player in a coma continues.
item.content:encoded:
Arizona State University has placed head coach of the men's hockey program Greg Powers on paid administrative leave as the school continues to investigate a workout that left a player in a coma.

Sophomore and St. Louis Blues prospect Matthew Mayich has been in a coma since the August 20 workout the team held, run by an ex-Army Green Beret.

On Wednesday, ASU athletic director Graham Rossini announced that Powers — who has led the program since it debuted at the D-1 level for the 2015-16 season — had been placed on leave the previous day.

FORMER MICHIGAN HOCKEY PLAYERS ALLEGE COACHES IGNORED YEARS OF ABUSIVE HAZING RITUALS

"Our focus continues to be on Matthew and his family, and on our student-athletes to make sure they have the support they need during this time and as the season begins," Rossini said in a statement. "We have continued to collect as much information as possible. After thorough and careful deliberation, I believe this is the best move to provide stability for the hockey program."

Assistant coach Mike Corbett will be behind the bench when the Sun Devils open their season on the road against Lindenwood University. An interim head coach will be named at a later date.

Powers' leave comes just days after seven members of the Sun Devil hockey program released a letter through an attorney that disputed certain findings of the school's initial review into the incident.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The 26-page letter sent to ASU President Michael Crow noted that the entire coaching staff — which was present at the workout — was, to that point, still with the program.

"The head coach and his assistant coaches were all on the field on August 20, all remain in their positions, and together they decide our playing time, scholarship levels, and roster status," the letter reads, per The Athletic. "No one has separated us from them since that morning.

"We should not have to choose between telling the truth about August 20 and keeping what we have worked our whole lives for."

Mayich remains in the hospital, with his family's attorney, Robert Carey, saying that he has "zero chance of recovery."

The 21-year-old transferred to Arizona State after playing last season at Clarkson University. He was selected by the Blues in the sixth round of the 2023 NHL Draft.

item.title: Biden Afghan migrant program hit with 40% vetting failure rate: 'Alarming'
item.description: A Homeland Security inspector general report found documentation or vetting errors in 40% of Afghan asylum applications reviewed under Operation Allies Welcome, raising concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Federal inspectors identified one or more documentation or vetting errors in 40% of asylum applications they reviewed for Afghan nationals admitted under the Biden administration's Operation Allies Welcome program, concluding the deficiencies increased the risk U. S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) could miss information that may have made some applicants ineligible for asylum.

The Sept. 23 Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of Inspector General report reviewed a sample of 678 asylum applications filed by Afghan nationals admitted through Operation Allies Welcome, the Biden administration initiative launched after the U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan. 

Inspectors identified 303 missing aliases, 23 missing security checks and more than 150 additional documentation deficiencies, including two cases involving applicants who may have been inadmissible on terrorism-related grounds.

FORMER USCIS OFFICIAL, ACCOMPLICE CHARGED IN ALLEGED $960K CITIZENSHIP BRIBERY SCHEME

The findings come as Operation Allies Welcome has faced renewed scrutiny following several high-profile arrests of Afghan nationals admitted under the program. 

Fox News Digital has previously reported on the arrests of an alleged ISIS-K supporter, an Afghan national charged with making terroristic threats and another Afghan national admitted under Operation Allies Welcome who was later arrested after being convicted of indecent exposure to a minor.

In a press release, DHS argued the report demonstrated the Biden administration "dangerously mismanaged" Operation Allies Welcome, saying a lawsuit settlement that required USCIS to adjudicate 90% of asylum applications within 150 days forced the agency to prioritize speed over more thorough reviews.

The DHS inspector general report, which noted hundreds of aliases had not been recorded for applicants, underscored the importance of accurate record keeping, pointing out one applicant had 124 known aliases. 

The report said that "missed FBI name checks" accounted for nearly 60% of the absent security checks that the report identified. 

The report also flagged two asylum applications involving applicants with potential terrorism-related concerns. In one case, required paperwork documenting the government's review was missing entirely. In another, supervisors began the approval process but never completed the final step, leaving no clear record that the review had been finished.

ARMY VET LAWMAKER MARKS ABBEY GATE ANNIVERSARY WITH BLISTERING MESSAGE FOR BIDEN-HARRIS: 'ABJECT FAILURE'

Mark Krikorian, executive director of the conservative Center for Immigration Studies, said the inspector general's findings reinforce concerns critics have raised since the chaotic Kabul evacuation in 2021.

"The fact that 40% of these applications have errors is alarming," Krikorian told Fox News Digital. "This IG report just underlines how superficial and even frivolous the vetting that we were assured was going on was."

Krikorian said many evacuees were first flown to temporary processing hubs, sometimes referred to as "lily pads," in third countries before ultimately being admitted to the United States. While those locations allowed U.S. officials to conduct additional processing, he argued the practical reality was that partner countries were not going to permanently accept the evacuees, leaving the United States effectively committed to resettling them.

HOMELAND SECURITY OFFICIAL'S KILLING LEAVES AGENCY 'DEVASTATED' AS VETTING BREAKDOWN EXPOSED

"As soon as that cargo bay door closed, we're stuck with those people," Krikorian said, noting how the United States effectively committed itself to resettling evacuees once they boarded evacuation flights during the chaotic Kabul withdrawal.

Krikorian argued the inspector general's report likely understated the scope of the problem because inspectors could only identify documentation deficiencies visible in the files they reviewed, not determine whether every applicant had been thoroughly vetted.

The inspector general ultimately made five recommendations aimed at strengthening USCIS' review of Operation Allies Welcome asylum applications, including improving documentation of applicant aliases, ensuring required security checks are properly recorded and enhancing oversight of adjudication files. 

USCIS agreed with all five recommendations, according to the report.

item.title: Fox News Poll: Michigan voters split between El-Sayed and Rogers
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed holds a slim 1-point edge over Mike Rogers in the Michigan senate race as voter concerns about both candidates keep it tight.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan voters have concerns about both candidates in the U.S. Senate race and that leads to a tight contest, according to a new Fox News poll.

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has a slim 1-point edge against Republican Mike Rogers, 50-49%, among Michigan likely voters. The survey, released on Wednesday, is the first Fox News Poll this season among likely voters, so a direct comparison can’t be made to previous polls.

Yet among registered voters, the preference is almost identical, 51% El-Sayed vs. 48% Rogers. That’s a reversal since August, when Rogers was ahead by 4 points among registered voters, 51% to El-Sayed’s 47%.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS QUESTION WHETHER AI’S PROMISE OUTWEIGHS ITS RISKS

The analysis below is among likely voters, unless otherwise noted.

More of El-Sayed’s backers feel certain of their choice (87%) than Rogers’ (80%). Overall, 15% say they could switch their pick before voting, including 18% of Rogers’ supporters and 12% of El-Sayed’s.

FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS

Here’s why the race is tight.

Roughly equal numbers of Michiganders say they are extremely concerned Rogers is too close to President Donald Trump (39%) as say El-Sayed’s views are too liberal (36%).

And their favorable ratings are also close: 47% view El-Sayed positively compared to 44% for Rogers. Among registered voters, positive views of El-Sayed increased by 5 points since August while Rogers’ declined by four points.

El-Sayed’s best groups include those who traditionally go Democratic: women, Black voters and those with a college degree. He’s also ahead with voters under age 45 and the small subgroup of union households.

The groups giving Rogers some of his strongest support include men, rural voters, White evangelical Christians, married voters and Whites without a college degree.

Both candidates receive near-universal backing from their party. Rogers receives 95% among Republicans, while it’s 93% for El-Sayed among Democrats. In addition, Rogers gets 99% of MAGA Republicans and 88% of non-MAGA Republicans, while El-Sayed garners 98% of DSA Democrats and 90% of non-DSA Democrats. The small number of independents narrowly favor El-Sayed.

This year’s political landscape favors El-Sayed. The Democrats hold a 5-point advantage when voters are asked which party they want to control the Senate, 52% to 47%. But to capitalize on that, he’ll need to consolidate Democratic support after a contentious primary because 11% of likely voters who backed his primary opponent Haley Stevens say they plan to vote for Rogers.

CLICK HERE FOR CROSSTABS AND TOPLINE

"The Michigan Senate race is unique in that short-term political forces favoring the Democrats are somewhat offset by concerns about the Democratic candidate," says Republican pollster Daron Shaw, who conducts the Fox News Poll with Democrat Chris Anderson. 

"The bad news for Rogers is El-Sayed has made progress shoring up Democratic support and has room to grow given voter concerns about the economy."

Four in ten Michiganders say they are falling behind financially, and they back El-Sayed by 25 points. But the largest share, nearly half, describe their family as holding steady, and they favor Rogers by 13 points, while the small number who are getting ahead prefer Rogers by 36 points.

Still, for 7 in 10 voters, the cost of living will be extremely important to their Senate vote, and they back El-Sayed by 13 points. He also has advantages among the 4 in 10 focused on U.S. policy toward Israel (+8 points) and AI technology (+17 points). Conversely, Rogers is favored by 26 points among the 44% focused on immigration.

Half of Michigan voters consider Trump extremely important to their Senate vote, and they favor El-Sayed by 22 points.

In 2024, Trump won Michigan by less than two percentage points, while Rogers lost to Democrat Elissa Slotkin by less than half a point.

Voter frustration with the administration is a drag on Rogers, as nearly 6 in 10 disapprove of the president’s performance. While 40% approve, not all support Rogers (93%). He remains competitive with support from 19% of Trump disapprovers overall, even as 28% who only "somewhat" disapprove of Trump prefer El-Sayed.

In the gubernatorial race to replace term-limited Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, Democrat Jocelyn Benson leads Republican John James 54% to 45% among likely voters.

Twelve percent of those backing Rogers in the Senate race cross-party lines to favor Benson.

Conducted September 24-28, 2026, under the joint direction of Beacon Research (D) and Shaw & Company Research (R), this Fox News Poll includes interviews with a sample of 1,203 Michigan registered voters randomly selected from a statewide voter file. Respondents spoke with live interviewers on landlines (114) and cellphones (794) or completed the survey online after receiving a text message (295). Results based on the registered voter sample have a margin of sampling error of ±2.5 percentage points and for the subsample of 1,028 likely voters it is ±3 percentage points. 

Sampling error for results among subgroups is higher. In addition to sampling error, question wording and order can influence results. Sources for developing weight targets include the most recent American Community Survey, Fox News Voter Analysis and voter file data. Weights are generally applied to age, race, education and area variables to ensure the demographics of respondents are representative of the registered voter population. Likely voters are based on a probabilistic statistical model that relies on past vote history, interest in the current election, intention to vote, age, education, race, ethnicity and marital status. Results among subgroups are only shown when the sample size is at least N=100. 

Fox News’ Victoria Balara contributed to this report.

item.title: Riley Gaines speaks out on dismissal of her lawsuit vs NCAA, hopes to take case to SCOTUS
item.description: Riley Gaines says she and fellow plaintiffs plan to appeal the NCAA lawsuit dismissal, hoping the Title IX case reaches the U.S. Supreme Court.
item.content:encoded:
Riley Gaines said the dismissal of her lawsuit against the NCAA could move the legal battle closer to what she hopes is its ultimate destination: the U.S. Supreme Court.

Gaines, joined by Independent Council on Women’s Sports co-founders Kim Jones and Marshi Smith, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive group interview that the plaintiffs will appeal after a federal judge granted summary judgment to the NCAA on their remaining Title IX claims.

"No instance of defeat or what is perceived or deemed as defeat feels good," Gaines said. "There [were] feelings of frustration, obviously, with the basis of what the grounds for dismissal was, indicating that the NCAA was not subject to Title IX."

RILEY GAINES' LAWSUIT VS NCAA DISMISSED BY BIDEN-APPOINTED JUDGE, APPEAL PLANNED

Smith said the first reaction among the other women involved in the lawsuit was "shock," particularly because the NCAA has frequently celebrated Title IX and its role in the growth of women’s college sports.

"The year that Riley was confronting this at the swim championships in 2022, it was the 50th-year anniversary of Title IX," Smith said. "The number of Title IX parties that the NCAA and each individual university threw for themselves, celebrating themselves for the success and triumph of Title IX."

Smith said the plaintiffs were stunned to see the NCAA successfully argue that it was not covered by the law it had publicly celebrated.

"To watch Riley compete against a 6-foot-4 male athlete that same year and have the NCAA celebrate him and his success in women’s sports, fast-forwarding to now, their complete denial of having any responsibility to Title IX — it’s mind-blowing," Smith said.

Jones described the other athletes as "bewildered" and "shell-shocked" by the outcome.

"This is an institution that we, as female athletes, have always believed had our backs, were bound by federal law [and] could not violate the rights of female athletes across the country," Jones said. "Even when I was going through school, the NCAA helped schools to ensure compliance to Title IX."

Jones argued that the NCAA’s structure makes the ruling especially difficult for the plaintiffs to accept. The organization is governed by representatives of its member institutions, many of which receive federal funding and are independently subject to Title IX.

"The NCAA is the controlling authority for collegiate athletics. They set nationwide policy. And the NCAA is composed of the schools," Jones said. "Their board of directors is presidents of universities."

WHAT THE SCOTUS TITLE IX RULING COULD MEAN FOR LAWSUITS SEEKING DAMAGES FOR WOMEN IMPACTED BY TRANS ATHLETES

However, Gaines said the athletes became more optimistic after considering the path ahead.

"Ultimately, this is something that I think myself and the dozens of other plaintiffs involved in the lawsuit would like to see before the Supreme Court," Gaines said. "That way it can be established, the law of the land once and for all, when it comes to female athletes and how large institutions like the NCAA are able to harm us with, at this point, little to zero accountability."

U.S. District Judge Tiffany R. Johnson ruled Monday that the evidence did not establish the NCAA as a recipient of federal financial assistance through its concussion-research collaboration with the Department of Defense. Because receiving federal assistance is required for liability under Title IX, Johnson entered judgment for the NCAA and closed the case.

The Biden-appointed judge did not determine whether the NCAA’s former transgender-athlete policy constituted sex discrimination.

The lawsuit was filed in 2024 by Gaines and more than a dozen other current and former female college athletes. It challenged NCAA policies that permitted biological males who met certain eligibility requirements to compete in women’s events.

The case focused heavily on the 2022 NCAA Division I Women’s Swimming and Diving Championships, where Gaines tied former University of Pennsylvania swimmer Lia Thomas for fifth place in the 200-yard freestyle. Thomas won the 500-yard freestyle national championship and used a women’s locker room during the event.

NCAA PRESIDENT CHARLIE BAKER REACTS TO SUPREME COURT RULING ON TRANSGENDER ATHLETES

That championship coincided with the 50th anniversary of Title IX, a detail Gaines and Smith said made the NCAA’s successful legal position particularly jarring.

"At that national championship, the NCAA was handing out shirts that said, you know, ‘50 years of Title IX creating opportunities for women,’" Gaines said. "The irony at the time, of course, being that they were making us compete against a 6-foot-4 man. But now here we are in this position, understanding that the NCAA is arguing that they’re not subject to Title IX."

Smith called the contrast "mind-blowing."

"The number of Title IX parties that the NCAA and each individual university threw for themselves, celebrating themselves for the success and triumph of Title IX," Smith said. "Fast-forwarding to now, their complete denial of having any responsibility to Title IX — it’s mind-blowing."

The NCAA responded to the dismissal by defending its current record on women’s athletics.

"The NCAA is proud to continually invest in and expand women’s sports and the NCAA is in full compliance with the Trump administration’s executive order on women’s sports," the organization said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

Gaines dismissed the response as "total hogwash" and accused the organization of invoking women’s sports only when convenient.

"It’s just a way to kind of wink at everyone, act as if they’re doing the right thing, the upstanding thing," Gaines said. "Again, pretending as if they care about women and their female athletes."

The NCAA changed its transgender participation policy in February 2025, one day after President Donald Trump signed his "Keeping Men Out of Women’s Sports" executive order. Its current rules prohibit athletes assigned male at birth from competing on women’s teams or receiving scholarships designated for women.

However, the policy permits those athletes to practice with women’s teams and receive other benefits available to athletes eligible for practice.

Smith argued that the NCAA’s statement did not offer female athletes a durable guarantee independent of the current administration.

"They have made absolutely no guarantees to women," Smith said. "They have not said, ‘We support female athletes and will not put men into women’s sports again.’"

Jones said the legal fight has left the plaintiffs feeling betrayed by an organization they once believed was responsible for protecting college athletes and promoting Title IX compliance, and hopes to take the lawsuit to the highest court.

"The goal of the young women is to — exactly what Riley said — take this all the way. There’s got to be accountability here." Jones said.

The plaintiffs have 30 days from the entry of judgment to file their notice of appeal with the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. Gaines said she remains confident that the case can eventually reach the nation’s highest court.

"There is light at the end of the tunnel," she said. "There is some optimism thinking forward about this case."

The dispute has also become intertwined with the 2026 midterm elections and the broader political fight over transgender participation in women’s sports.

Gaines said she expected Democrats to distance themselves from transgender-athlete policies after Republicans’ success in the 2024 election. Instead, she argued, the party has remained committed to positions she believes contributed to its electoral losses.

"I really was under the impression that we would begin to see Democrats slowly start to recant, or distance themselves from their previous voting records, or statements, or things, that they’ve said when it comes to women’s rights and our safety and privacy and equal opportunities in our sports and beyond," Gaines said. "But that’s just not at all what they’ve done."

Gaines cited Democratic proposals to expand the Supreme Court as one political development that could affect the lawsuit if it takes several years to reach the justices.

"Even beyond this issue, that concerns me. Of course it does," Gaines said. "That’s just one of many things across many different issues that the Democrats have promised to do and have campaigned on doing, which is why I believe there is such an emphasis on this November and what midterms really look like."

She urged parents to consider issues involving school sports, parental rights, education and student privacy when they vote.

"If you have daughters, if you have kids, if you’re a parent, and you care about your parental rights and your children and their education and their success and their well-being and their health and their safety and their privacy and their opportunities, that enough should be a motivating factor to get out to the ballot box in November," Gaines said.

Gaines acknowledged that the debate has become heavily partisan, but said the athletes challenging the NCAA did not originally view the protection of women’s sports as an inherently political cause.

"We don’t view this issue as a political issue," Gaines said. "We have called on those on the other side of the aisle to link arms, to stand with us, but that just hasn’t been the case."

She characterized policies allowing biological males to enter women’s sports as a reversal of the progress female athletes secured through Title IX.

"What’s happening now is taking us back to that time," Gaines said. "It’s not progressive, it’s regressive."

item.title: Staggering drug haul found at major airport after bizarre attempt to hide evidence
item.description: Orlando International Airport police and K-9s intercepted over 200 pounds of marijuana allegedly smuggled on commercial flights from Los Angeles. A security expert shares context.
item.content:encoded:
More than 200 pounds of marijuana reportedly made its way onto commercial flights from Los Angeles to Orlando International Airport (MCO) this summer — before police intercepted the drugs in two separate airport busts.

The smugglers allegedly attempted to bring hundreds of pounds of bulk marijuana into Central Florida from Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), according to police records recently obtained by FOX 35 Orlando.

The drugs were intercepted by undercover officers with the Orlando Police Department (OPD) and drug-sniffing K-9s, FOX 35 reported.

ONE CANNABIS MISTAKE AT AIRPORT COULD BRING 10 YEARS IN PRISON AND $15,000 FINE

Investigators said the suspects used superglue and ripped-off luggage tags to try to evade police, as well as dryer sheets to conceal the smell of marijuana.

During one bust, which occurred on May 7, officers found 57.6 pounds of marijuana packed inside 50 vacuum-sealed bags, wrapped in blankets and stuffed with dryer sheets, according to the report.

In a second bust on July 1, police found 144.4 pounds of marijuana in suitcases with locks that had been completely glued shut.

FOX 35 identified the suspects as individuals in their 20s who are now facing felony drug trafficking charges.

TSA OFFICER SEES ALARMING SHAPES ON X-RAY BEFORE STOLEN CIVIL WAR MYSTERY UNRAVELS

Keith Jeffries, vice president of K2 Security Screening Group, told Fox News Digital that drug smuggling on commercial flights "can happen in multiple ways."

Those scenarios could include airport or airline employees assisting smugglers or traffickers using drug mules, he said — though he cautioned that it remains unclear how the drugs made it onto the flights in these cases.

Jeffries also said law enforcement may have been tipped off about certain individuals or bags by a confidential informant.

"It's unknown at this time without talking to law enforcement and getting the specifics," he said.

Jeffries, who previously served as TSA's federal security director at LAX and deputy federal security director at MCO, added that drug trafficking "can happen on any domestic route — and it does."

He said Orlando's status as a major tourist destination, in particular, could make the city attractive to traffickers.

"The illegal perpetrators in this [situation] may think and believe that, well, the security must be lax there, which is not the case," Jeffries said.

He also noted that TSA officers do not specifically search for illegal drugs, and that suspected narcotics discovered during screening are referred to law enforcement.

"The TSA's administrative search authority is very, very narrow and very specific," Jeffries said.

"TSA does not look for illegal narcotics," he added. "They simply say, 'We've got an unknown substance, and we need law enforcement's attention so that law enforcement can validate what it is or is not.'"

Fox News Digital reached out to the Orlando Police Department for additional information.

While the Orlando marijuana was intercepted by local law enforcement, TSA officers have made other unusual discoveries during airport screenings in recent weeks.

Earlier in September, TSA officers at Dallas Love Field Airport in Texas discovered a pocketknife concealed inside a tube of toothpaste during routine carry-on screening.

In Tampa, TSA officers recently discovered a 4-inch, double-edged knife concealed inside a baseball bat-shaped flashlight in a passenger's carry-on bag.
